A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CAD-Assistant and contain readable main texts and complete supplementary Sections 7–15. Text and visual inspection support reliable comparison of the methods, equations, results, and appendices.

before.justification: v2 reports original CAD question-answering, autoconstraining, and hand-drawn sketch parameterization experiments in Tables 2–6, with additional qualitative results in the supplement.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and adds human assessments of failure types and tool-use validity in Section 4.3.

M1.justification: The VLLM planner, iterative Python/FreeCAD execution, feedback mechanism, and CAD-specific tools remain unchanged. Equations (1)–(4), the supplementary prompt, and complete tool docstrings disclose the same procedure despite shortened method prose.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same SGPBench 2D/3D tasks, SketchGraphs autoconstraining and hand-drawn parameterization, and multimodal qualitative scenarios. The new human assessments examine trajectories from existing tasks without adding data domains or task requirements.

E2.justification: Comparator membership remains unchanged: the three GPT baselines for CQA, GPT-4o and Vitruvion for autoconstraining, and Vitruvion and Davinci for hand-drawn parameterization. The representation comparisons in Table 2 are also retained.

E3.justification: v3 introduces human evaluation protocols: one annotator categorizes 100 misclassified CQA trajectories, and two annotators assess tool-use validity in 200 autoconstraining/parameterization trajectories. No corresponding change to the existing benchmark procedures or planner versions is documented.

E4.justification: Section 4.3 adds a targeted failure analysis identifying categories of CQA errors and an audit testing whether tools are used validly. Existing representation, tool, and prompting ablations, along with supplementary correction and qualitative examples, remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new human assessments report sample and annotator counts but add no uncertainty estimates or inter-annotator agreement statistics.

E6.justification: Table 3 revises CAD-Assistant's 3D accuracies from 0.737 to 0.783 for GPT-4 mini, 0.789 to 0.825 for GPT-4 Turbo, and 0.805 to 0.857 for GPT-4o; baseline and 2D values remain unchanged. v3 also adds the Figure 4 error distribution and 98.5% tool-use validity. The PDFs do not explain the accuracy revisions.

T1.justification: The framework equations and supplementary definitions of sketches, constraints, primitive parameterizations, and extrusion parameters remain unchanged, including Tables 7–10. No mathematical assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: Both versions retain the central claims of a general-purpose, training-free, extensible, tool-augmented CAD agent with multimodal capabilities and zero-shot benchmark advantages. Edits to the abstract, related work, and conclusion do not materially redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: The new human-evaluation discussion attributes CQA failures primarily to reasoning and misinterpretation of renderings, including confusing a trapezoid with a triangle. It attributes rare invalid tool use primarily to FreeCAD API misuse, adding specific failure explanations to the existing limitations.

D1.justification: v3 adds a public-code availability statement and repository link in the abstract, but removes the explicit 1,000-model count for the 3D CQA subset. DeepCAD provenance remains in supplementary Section 9.2, and model identifiers, costs, prompts, and tool docstrings are retained.

R1.justification: Section 2 removes the animal-tool-behavior analogy and its citation to Shumaker, Walkup, and Beck. The remaining CAD and tool-augmentation literature and substantive novelty positioning are retained; subsequent reference-number changes reflect this deletion.

P1.justification: v3 trims introductory and related-work prose, removes the paper roadmap, shortens explanatory passages and the conclusion, and renames Section 4.3 to Experimental Results. These are localized edits; the main narrative and supplementary organization remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds the failure-category bar chart as Figure 4, renumbering the retained real-world and supplementary figures. It relocates Table 2, shortens several captions, adjusts figure placement and sizing, and removes printed page numbers while preserving the overall layout.

improvement.justification: The added human assessments provide useful evidence about failure mechanisms and tool-use reliability, while the implementation link improves access information. These targeted gains are tempered by unexplained Table 3 revisions, removal of the 3D sample count, and retained text calling GPT-4 mini's 3D performance 'on-par' despite the revised 0.783 versus 0.737 comparison.
